author: Yffe
content:
Failing tests at forge/tests/divergence_forge.rs::divergence_multi_item_correct_item_not_falsely_failed and ::divergence_multi_item_counterexample_misattributed demonstrate the divergence.

ROOT CAUSE: check::check_file runs verus ONCE on the whole lowered crate, producing a single crate-level VerusResult, then assemble_certificate(item, &verus) copies that same {level, obligations} into EVERY item's certificate. When any item fails verus, ALL items inherit level L0 and the same failed obligation.

REPRO: a 2-item .th file where good (ens result==x+x over body x+x, holds for all inputs) and bad (false ens). forge check reports good as level=L0 with obligation 'postcondition not satisfied @ <bad's lowered span>'. good's contract references nothing in bad.

AUTHORITY:
- thermite-design.md §5.3: 'an edit to f cannot invalidate g's certificate unless g's contract references f's contract.' good is invalidated by bad with no contract dependency.
- thermite-design.md §6: 'The certificate ... lists every function's level' — a correct function must list its own L3 level.
- thermite-design.md §5.1: 'counterexamples, not adjectives' — good's cert carries a concrete witness (a source span) that belongs to bad; a misattributed witness asserts a falsehood.
- goal.md R-SPEC-2 (the certificate is a contract), R-HONEST-3 (a correct item reported as failing is an honesty divergence).

The builder's commit flagged 'per-obligation results are crate-level not per-item' as a schema decision, but this is not additive schema surface — it produces a factually WRONG certificate (correct item reported L0). NOT a blocker only for multi-item-fail mix: the all-pass and single-item cases are correct; the mixed case is wrong.
